scenes.line1: What does a Dockerfile really do?
scenes.say: Ever wonder how Docker knows what to put in your image? Let's break down the Dockerfile.

scenes.label: Layers
scenes.sub: Each instruction in a Dockerfile adds a new image layer.
scenes.say: Each line in your Dockerfile adds a layer to your image. Layers make builds faster and more efficient.

scenes.code:
FROM python:3.12-slim
WORKDIR /app
COPY requirements.txt .
RUN pip install --no-cache-dir -r requirements.txt
COPY . .
USER 1000
EXPOSE 8000
CMD ["gunicorn", "-b", "0.0.0.0:8000", "app:app"]
scenes.say: Here's a real Dockerfile. It sets the base image, copies dependencies, installs them, then adds your code.
Copy your dependency file before your code. That way, Docker can cache the install step if only your code changes.

scenes.question: Does changing code bust the pip cache?
scenes.right: Yes, if code is copied before deps, the install step reruns.
scenes.say: Here's a trap: If you copy your code before your dependencies, Docker will rerun pip install every time you change your code. That slows you down.
